title: A good element is a nonzerodivisor and its quotient is Cohen-Macaulay with a shorter maximal regular sequence
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a good element g with respect to a tuple (M, f_1, ..., f_d) is a nonzerodivisor on M and that M/gM is Cohen-Macaulay with maximal regular sequence f_1, ..., f_{d-1} (statement lines 25201-25207). The proof does not rework the definition of goodness: in the case d = 1 it bounds the support of the kernel of multiplication by g to the closed point, so that the kernel has finite length and Nakayama kills it; in general it observes that g stays good on M/f_1M, applies the induction hypothesis, and permutes the resulting regular sequence with f_1 (proof lines 25209-25232). Recognising that the hypothesis descends to the quotient by f_1 is what makes the induction work. H2.
